rounds.proof_sketch: M=1024, BLOCK_SIZE=16, gridDim.y=64. Max A_row = 63*16+15 = 1023 < M=1024. The condition A_row < M vs A_row <= M is always true for all A_row in [0,1023]. The boundary case A_row==M is unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the bounds check from A_row < M to A_row <= M when loading tiles from matrix A. However, with M=1024 and BLOCK_SIZE=16, the grid is sized to exactly cover all rows (64 blocks × 16 threads = 1024 threads covering rows 0-1023). Since A_row is always in [0, 1023] and M=1024, both conditions A_row < 1024 and A_row <= 1024 evaluate to true for every thread. The edge case where A_row == M would trigger an out-of-bounds read is architecturally unreachable with this fixed shape.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable with fixed shapes. Would require M to be non-divisible by BLOCK_SIZE (e.g., M=1025) so that some threads have row >= M. Since shapes cannot change per the contract, no value-level input can trigger the difference.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should consider whether boundary conditions depend on tensor shapes vs values. When testing relational operator mutations in bounds checks, ensure test shapes include non-tile-aligned dimensions to expose boundary behavior differences.
